An update to n2den, the experimental Nintendo Switch 2 recompulator built on Eden.

n2den runs decrypted dumps of games you own. It contains no decryption code, does not use console keys, and includes no games.

## Downloads

| Package | What it is |
|---|---|
| `n2Den-v1.0.4-windows-x64-pgo.zip` | **Recommended.** Built with clang, ThinLTO and a profile trained on gameplay: the faster build. The command-line `n2Den-cli.exe` is only in the MSVC package. |
| `n2Den-v1.0.4-windows-x64.zip` | The same source built with MSVC, like the test builds. Use it if the PGO build misbehaves on your machine. |
| `*-symbols.zip` | Debug symbols for crash reports. Not needed to play. |

Windows x64 with a Vulkan GPU. Extract into a new folder; create an empty `user` folder beside `n2Den.exe` for portable mode. You can extract over 1.0.3 or keep both side by side.

## What's new since 1.0.3

### NVN-HLE is now the default

- Switch 2 games now run on **NVN-HLE** unless you choose otherwise. It is faster in most games and is the backend the tested games have been checked on. The **Emulated GPU** stays available per game (game properties, GPU backend). A game you already set to the Emulated GPU keeps that setting.

### New game

- **Kirby Air Riders** is now playable on NVN-HLE: title screen, attract demo, races and rider showcases, with a correct picture.

### Graphics

- Fixed the GPU hanging when a Kirby Air Riders race starts. NVIDIA's shader compiler mis-built one form of guarded shared-memory load the game's compute shaders use; those loads are now translated in a form it compiles correctly.
- Fixed black shadows: compute shaders that read separate textures and samplers got the wrong handles, so the per-model light bake wrote nothing and lit areas in shadow stayed black.
- Fixed black characters in shade: texture handles that a compute shader looks up in a table at run time are now resolved per thread, so the light probes that light characters are read.
- Fixed a washed-out picture (grey blacks, low contrast) when NVIDIA DLSS replaces a game's own upscaling network that ends in linear colour. The default upscaler, Console native, was not affected.
- Shader translation fixes for bindless texture fetches, uniform-register selects and larger jump tables.

### Memory and loading

- Pipelines saved from earlier sessions are now built when first used instead of all at boot, so games with a large shader cache start faster and use less memory.
- Compute pipelines that a command list will dispatch next are compiled ahead, to reduce stalls.

## Tested games

| Game | Emulated GPU | NVN-HLE (Vulkan) |
|---|---|---|
| The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (Switch 2) | In-game | In-game |
| Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave | In-game | In-game |
| Fast Fusion | Playable | Playable |
| Kirby and the Forgotten Land – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Star-Crossed World | Playable | Playable |
| Donkey Kong Bananza | In-game | In-game |
| Kirby Air Riders | Boots | Playable |
| Orbitals Deluxe Edition | Not usable | In-game, slow |
| Xenoblade Chronicles 2 – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition | Not tested | In-game |
| Xenoblade Chronicles: Definitive Edition – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition | Not tested | In-game |
| Nintendo Switch Sports Resort | Not tested | Boots |
| Mario Kart World | Not tested | Unstable |

Details and known issues per game: [docs/GameProgress.md](https://github.com/Duck912/n2den/blob/main/docs/GameProgress.md). Games not in the table have not been tested.

## Known issues

- Expect missing graphics and crashes: this is a development release.
- The first start of each game after updating is slower and stutters for a while: the shader cache is rebuilt once. Kirby Air Riders also stutters when a new scene compiles its shaders.
- In Xenoblade Chronicles 2 a fine grid shows over the picture when the Resolution setting is above 1X; keep it at 1X. The game also uses a lot of video memory.
- Games in large `.nup` containers take a while to load because their data is unpacked at every start.
- Mario Kart World can run out of system RAM after several minutes and is not recommended for play.
- Only Windows is supported for now.

## Reporting problems

Open an issue with `user\log\eden_log.txt` (or `%APPDATA%\eden\log\eden_log.txt`), taken right after the problem, plus your GPU and driver version.
